research_question: Can additional capacity in a locked Q.ANT-native Fourier/KAN architecture close part of the Fashion-MNIST accuracy gap to the h64_512 ReLU control while retaining a substantial parameter advantage?
observations: Exp010 placed qfourier_g1 and qfourier_g2 on the accuracy-versus-parameter Pareto front, but their mean Q.ANT accuracies (0.8068 and 0.8225) remained below h64_512 (0.8596).
Increasing grid_size from 1 to 2 improved mean Q.ANT accuracy by about 1.57 percentage points while increasing trainable parameters from 15,690 to 31,370.
QFourier showed materially larger PyTorch-reference versus Q.ANT prediction disagreement (124-390 of 10,000) than the ReLU controls (2-15).
hypothesis: Increasing QFourier capacity with pre-registered grid sizes 4 and 8 will improve mean Q.ANT-backend accuracy beyond qfourier_g2, and at least one candidate will remain Pareto-efficient relative to h64_512 while using fewer trainable parameters.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if neither larger-grid QFourier candidate improves mean Q.ANT accuracy over qfourier_g2, or if both are dominated by h64_512 and/or smaller QFourier candidates on mean Q.ANT accuracy and parameter count. Large growth in reference-to-Q.ANT disagreement will also count against the practical usefulness of the added capacity.

proposed_method.training_reference: Train amplitude/phase parameters with exact torch.cos and no injected training noise; evaluate QFourier through qant.ai.calc_kan_layer_fprop on the Q.ANT CPU backend.

limitations: Q.ANT CPU backend only; no claim about photonic latency, energy, throughput, or optical-hardware performance.
Fashion-MNIST, three seeds, and three epochs limit generality and precision.
Exact cosine training and Q.ANT periodic evaluation are not identical; disagreement is therefore a primary metric.
The architecture family and grid sizes are locked before Exp011 execution to avoid post-hoc tuning.
